title: Session Ribbons: Contextual Dock Prototype & Usability Review for Console Navigation
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Problem: Console users report friction when switching context between monitoring dashboards, rollout controls, and cost breakdowns. Current sidebar exposes a single persistent nav that forces users to open multiple pages to correlate rollout status with token-level cost.

Objective: Prototype a "session ribbons" pattern (branded here as Contextual Dock) that dynamically surfaces workspace-relevant routes (dashboards, rollouts, cost lenses, recent traces) in a condensed dock attached to the primary sidebar. The dock should reduce clicks for common tasks (compare rollout state vs. cost impact, surface per-route latency histograms) and support fast workspace switching without leaving the current detail view.

Scope: This ticket covers design exploration, high-fidelity mockups, prototype flows for desktop, lightweight keyboard and screenreader guidance, and two moderated usability sessions. Work will culminate in a design handoff package and prioritized dev tasks.

Non-goals: Full mobile redesign, backend telemetry schema changes, or implementation of cost calculations (those are covered by ENG-4412).
acceptance_criteria: Contextual Dock prototype (desktop) available in Figma with 3 example contexts: Dashboard, Rollouts, Cost Lens
Prototype demonstrates: dock reveal (hover/chevron), pin/unpin state, workspace quick-switch, and an inline rollout summary card
Usability results from 2 moderated sessions with at least 6 participants total; documented insights and recommended adjustments
Design tokens, spacing, and keyboard focus states documented for dev handoff
Accessibility notes (ARIA roles, announcements for dock expand/collapse) included
Handoff includes annotated flows and a prioritized list of dev tickets (minimum: ENG-4412, ENG-4413)
comments: 2026-03-01 Priya Nair: Posted initial concept and rationale. Figma file created: https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/session-ribbons-contextual-dock (see frames: 'Dock-Exploration', 'Dock-Pinned', 'Dock-Compact')

2026-03-02 Ethan Cole (Eng): Reviewed. Engineering constraint: continuous streaming responses cause route hydration delays; need a fallback when dock requests exceed 200ms. Marking ENG-4412 for runtime gating.
2026-03-03 Maya Patel (PM): Love the inline rollout card. Request: show 'last-seen' latency and cost delta in the summary. Added to scope as an optional enhancement.

2026-03-05 Usability researcher (Liam O.) : Two remote moderated sessions scheduled (3/6 and 3/7). Recruit notes: 2 infra engineers, 2 product engineers, 2 growth PMs. Tasks: find rollout status, compare cost delta across two routes, switch to dedicated capacity view.

2026-03-07 Liam O.: Sessions complete. Key findings: (1) participants found the dock's compact affordance reduced context-switch time by ~40% versus left nav baseline; (2) 'pin' discoverability low — added persistent chevron and tooltip; (3) keyboard users expected Cmd/Ctrl+K to open workspace switcher in-context. See research notes: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/CONSOLE/Session+Ribbons+Research

2026-03-07 Priya Nair: Iterated prototype to add explicit keyboard hint, improved focus outline, and compact rollout microcard with cost delta. Updated Figma: /proto and added annotations for ARIA roles.

2026-03-08 Ethan Cole: Prepared initial dev spike PR to add dock container and lazy-load metrics widgets (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-console/pull/4821). Noted: need telemetry gating for dashboards to avoid extra cold-starts.

2026-03-08 Product review: PM asked to prioritize rollouts card and cost delta as first rollout. Marking dependent tickets: ENG-4412 (runtime gating), ENG-4413 (rollout microcard API), PM-782 (rollout metrics contract).
ux_research: Method: 2 moderated remote sessions, task-based, think-aloud
Participants: 6 (mix of infra, product and platform engineers)
Top pain points discovered: persistent nav forces full page context switch; rollout->cost correlation requires 3 clicks; low discoverability for pin/unpin state
decisions: Ship dock as a progressive enhancement: default collapsed on first-run, users may pin to persist; implementation must not change existing URLs
Show a compact rollout microcard with name, status (green/yellow/red), last-deploy time, and 24h cost delta
Expose workspace quick-switcher inside dock with recent-workspaces history and keyboard shortcut hint
Accessibility: dock expand/collapse uses aria-expanded on button and a live region for updates to rollout summary
